question: How does the Lord originate all beings from the great Brahman womb?
premises: My womb is the great Brahman; in it I place the seed; thence comes the birth of all beings.
Abhinava: the unspeakable bliss-form's own expanding power takes up the reflective power over beginningless atoms for grace.
Thus I set them transmigrating — abandonment of the cause, once known, is easy.
inference: Creation is the Lord's self-power sowing seed in the Brahman-womb; knowing this cause makes release easy.
uncertainties: Prose compounds on vimarśa-śakti and śakti-rūpa segmented by sense; Abhinava's technical terms kept literal.
plain_english: My womb is the great Brahman; in it I place the seed; thence comes the birth of all beings, O Bhārata. For what is to be abandoned, once its cause is known, is easy — I, of unspeakable bliss-form, taking up my own expanding power as Brahman, my reflective power over beginningless atoms, set them transmigrating for grace.
